title: ID0425799-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / P7 170000786 ]  interruptions while charging
description:
Reported issue: The charger only sporadically delivers full power when the vehicle is connected alone. There are several interruptions in the charging process. Restarting is not always possible. The vehicles were swapped and tested at other charging stations to rule out a fault in the vehicle. At other fast chargers, it can be charged immediately at 100kW.
Solution:
yyyy-mm-dd:
80kw Limited = optimization → v8
charging interrupted 13th → ERR69 → install EcoG 1.4.12
14th May → SoC = 100%

additional_info.subject: ID0425799-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / P7 170000786 ]  interruptions while charging CRM:02684000269
additional_info.body:
Hello Sven, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
I searched for the logs in the timestamps you provided and here are my findings:
For the charging sessions that are only providing 80kW, we have a logic made for public charging which is the following:
When the session starts, if the electric vehicle has more than 40% SoC, and takes more than 1min to reach maximum power:
The charger removes some power in case it's needed to charger another electric vehicle in parallel.
For this, we expecting a fix on the next version v8.
For the session on the 13th May where it unexpectedly stopped, we have a hotfix for this error, which is related to a timeout. If I have your permission, I can install the latest FW version v7.0.5 and install the hotfix with it.
For the last topic which is during 14th May where it didn't charge, I can see in the logs that the EV is actually full, 100% SoC:
As you can see, since the EV was full, it was only requesting 1 A.
I will wait patiently for your feedback.
Thank you and have a nice day!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0425799-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / P7 170000786 ]  interruptions while charging CRM:02684000269
additional_info.body:
Hallo Sven, good morning.
Thank you for raising your questions. I will try to answer as best as possible. Please let me know if you didn't understand something.
The reason why we have this logic is because the Sicharge D was initially created for Public charging only and did not forsee Depot charging.
Let me explain using an example, following the logic and specifications of your Sicharge D:
Your Sicharge D has a maximum power of 160kW divided by 2 connectors.
If only 1 connector is charging it
can
provide 160kW.
If 2 connectors are charging at the same time, each one
can
get 80kW.
When a electric vehicle reaches 40% SoC, the ramp down of power occurs.
In order to allow another electric vehicle to charge, because if 1 EV is charging with 160kW , the 2nd EV won't charge at all.
Example:
EV1 reaches the Sicharge D and starts charging with 20% SoC with 160kW. When it reaches 40% SoC, the system releases 80kW to allow EV2 to charge when it reaches the charger. This way we can have 2 EVs charging instead of just 1.
For the update, it is required to be free, no charging process ongoing.
It takes around 30 minutes to perform the update. After the update is completed, I will apply the hotfix which takes around 10 minutes.
Please let me know if you have any schedules where no one charges or if I can start the update as soon as no charging process is ongoing.
Thank you and have a nice day.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0425799-DC/Si-D/DE-[ MP / P7 170000786 ]  interruptions while charging CRM:02684000269
additional_info.body:
Hallo Sven,
F:
Ich habe nochmal eine Frage zur neuen Software V8.
Es wird dann mit mehr als 80kW geladen, wenn der SoC-Level des Fahrzeugs über 80% ist? Das kann dann nicht mehr passieren?
Entschuldige bitte, dass ich nochmal frage, aber ich will sicher gehen, dass ich es richtig übersetzt und verstanden habe.
A: Wird weiterhin mit mehr als 80kW geladen, wenn der SoC-Level des Fahrzeugs über 80% liegt? Das kann nicht mehr passieren? -> Ja wird dann nicht mehr Passieren.
F: Dann habe ich noch eine Frage. Ist es möglich die Ladesäule so zu programmieren, dass sie flexibel wird?
Ich meine damit, dass die Ladeleistung bei einem Fahrzeug (EV1) erhöht wird wenn beim anderen (EV2) die Leistung runtergeht, weil der Akku sich 100% nähert.
A: Das hängt vom Elektrofahrzeug ab. Wenn das Fahrzeug sich langsam den 100% nähert und den Strom reduziert, geschieht dies automatisch.
Erfahrungsgemäß zum Beispiel reduzieren MAN-Busse den Ladestrom nicht basierend auf dem SOC - sie fordern immer die maximale Leistung bis 100% an, daher würde es hier nicht funktionieren. Volvo reduziert zwar etwas, aber ehrlich gesagt nicht besonders viel. Kommt immer auf das Fahrzeug an. Aber man könnte per Smartchargingprofiles ein Profil erstellen der den Ladestrom je nach SOC steuert. Dazu sollten sie sich an ihr Backend wenden.
Thank you.
With best regards,
Semih Sentürk
eMobility Tech Support Team
